title: Crash at exit whenever a `CanvasTexture` RID is leaked: `~CanvasTexture` invokes its invalidation callback after `RendererCanvasRender::singleton` is nulled
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.2.stable [ed1daf0bf], 4.7.1.stable, 4.7.stable, 4.6.stable — all exit with code 134 (`handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11`).
- Not reproducible in: 4.3.stable — the same project leaks the `CanvasTexture` at exit but shuts down cleanly (exit 0).
- Not tested: 4.4.x and 4.5.x (not installed here). The callback involved was introduced by 663917449b ("2D: Fix `CanvasTexture` rendering when updating channels", #101931), first released in 4.4-stable, so I would expect the regression range to start there.
- Reproducible in a self-built current master, 4.8.dev [944a3c6cbb] (macOS, Metal, `vulkan=no`), which is where I confirmed the fix: unpatched that build exits 134, and with the change described below the same build exits 0.

### System information

macOS 27.0 (26A5406e) - Godot v4.7.2.stable - Forward+ (Metal 4.0) - Apple M3 Pro (Apple9, 12 threads)

### Issue description

If a `CanvasTexture` RID is still allocated at engine shutdown, Godot crashes 100% of the time with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` / `SIGSEGV` at a small fixed address (`0xb38` on this build). It happens on quit, on editor restart, and on "exit to project list" — anything that runs `Main::cleanup()`.

The chain:

1. `~TextureStorage` destroys its `RID_Owner<CanvasTexture, true> canvas_texture_owner`.
2. `~RID_Alloc` (`core/templates/rid_owner.h`) reports the leak and then runs `~T()` on every leaked element.
3. `TextureStorage::CanvasTexture::~CanvasTexture()` fires `invalidated_callback(true, invalidated_callback_userdata)`.
4. That callback is `RendererCanvasRenderRD::_canvas_texture_invalidation_callback`, which does:

```cpp
	if (p_deleted) {
		static_cast<RendererCanvasRenderRD *>(singleton)->canvas_texture_to_uniform_set.erase(kv->key);
	}
```

`RendererCanvasRender::singleton` is already `nullptr` by then. `RendererCompositorRD::finalize()` deletes the canvas renderer seven lines before the texture storage that still holds its callback registration:

```cpp
void RendererCompositorRD::finalize() {
	texture_storage->_tex_blit_shader_free();
	memdelete(scene);
	memdelete(canvas);          // ~RendererCanvasRender sets singleton = nullptr (renderer_canvas_render.h:558)
	...
	memdelete(texture_storage); // ~RID_Owner<CanvasTexture> -> ~CanvasTexture -> the stale callback
	...
}
```

So the callback ends up doing `HashMap::erase()` on `nullptr + offsetof(RendererCanvasRenderRD, canvas_texture_to_uniform_set)`, which matches the faulting address being a small constant.

`~RendererCanvasRenderRD` already clears this callback for `default_canvas_texture`, with the comment "Disable the callback, as we're tearing everything down" (`renderer_canvas_render_rd.cpp:3402`) — it just doesn't do it for the canvas textures tracked in `canvas_texture_to_uniform_set`.

Two knock-on effects worth noting:

- The abort happens *before* the ObjectDB leak dump, so the "N ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit (run with `--verbose` for details)" report and its `Leaked instance:` lines never print. The crash hides exactly the diagnostics a user needs to find their own leak.
- Because the macOS release binary is stripped, the engine's own backtrace prints misleading symbols (everything resolves to `SDL_GetPerformanceFrequency`), which makes this look unrelated to rendering in user-submitted reports.

Compatibility/GLES3 has no equivalent invalidation callback on its `CanvasTexture`, so this is specific to the RD renderers (Forward+/Mobile). GLES3 users report the same leak without the crash.

This is the same class of problem as #85520 ("Avoid crashes when engine leaks canvas items and friends") — leaked-at-exit cleanup reaching into an already-torn-down subsystem.

Symbolising the macOS crash report against the official 4.7.2 binary (load address subtracted) gives:

| frame | offset | function |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | +0x425EDEC | `HashMap::_lookup_pos` (faults on its first instruction, `ldr x8, [x0]`) |
| 1 | +0x425AAB8 | `HashMap::erase` |
| 2 | +0x43C50F8 | `RID_Alloc<CanvasTexture>::~RID_Alloc` — return address of the `blr` in the inlined `~CanvasTexture` |
| 3 | +0x43B2E24 | `TextureStorage::~TextureStorage` |
| 4 | +0x42614FC | `RendererCompositorRD::finalize()` |
| 5 | +0x417B9F4 | `RenderingServerDefault::_finish()` |
| 6-7 | +0x74DCD8, +0x772C00 | `Main::cleanup()` |

I originally hit this in a real project, where a third-party addon leaks a `TileSet` graph including its `CanvasTexture`s, and got byte-identical crash reports across 4.7.1 and 4.7.2. A likely-related third-party report on Windows/Forward+ is pablogila/TileMapDual#73, which suggests this is not platform-specific, though that reporter's backtrace has no symbols to confirm it.

**Proposed fix.** Clear the callback for every canvas texture the renderer tracks in `~RendererCanvasRenderRD`, extending what it already does for `default_canvas_texture`:

```cpp
	for (const KeyValue<RID, TightLocalVector<RID>> &E : canvas_texture_to_uniform_set) {
		texture_storage->canvas_texture_set_invalidation_callback(E.key, nullptr, nullptr);
	}
```

That removes the dangling registration at the source. A null check on `singleton` at the top of `_canvas_texture_invalidation_callback` is worth adding as well, since neither it nor `RenderingDevice` can service the callback once teardown has started. I have both on a branch and will open a PR.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a blank project and attach the script below to the main scene's root `Node2D`.
2. Run the project — the sprite must actually be drawn at least once, because the callback is only registered while batching a `CanvasTexture` (`renderer_canvas_render_rd.cpp:3039`). A leaked-but-never-drawn `CanvasTexture` has a null callback and exits cleanly.
3. Quit.

```
ERROR: 1 RID allocations of type 'N10RendererRD14TextureStorage7TextureE' were leaked at exit.
ERROR: 1 RID allocations of type 'N10RendererRD14TextureStorage13CanvasTextureE' were leaked at exit.
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
```

Scriptable as `godot --path <mrp> --quit-after 120; echo $?` → 134 on 4.6+, 0 on 4.3.

The reference cycle in the script is only there to force the leak deterministically; any leaked `CanvasTexture` will do, and in the real project the leak came from ordinary addon code rather than anything deliberate.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not project dependent — a blank project plus one script reproduces it, so there is nothing meaningful to attach. In full, `main.gd`:

```gdscript
extends Node2D


func _ready() -> void:
	var ct := CanvasTexture.new()
	ct.diffuse_texture = GradientTexture2D.new()
	var s := Sprite2D.new()
	s.texture = ct
	s.position = Vector2(200, 200)
	add_child(s)
	# Deliberate reference cycle: leaks the CanvasTexture at exit.
	ct.set_meta("cycle", ct)
```

`main.tscn` is a single `Node2D` named `Main` with that script attached, and `project.godot` only sets `config/name` and `run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"`.
